newsitem.title: CROATIA: Yugoslav foreign minister to visit Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav foreign minister to visit Croatia.

text.p: Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic will go to Croatia on Tuesday on his first official visit under a normalisation treaty solidifying peace in the Balkans, Croatian state radio said on Monday.

It said Milutinovic and Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic would discuss steps to implement the treaty along with humanitarian and trade issues. Milutinovic would also have talks with Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
Granic and Milutinovic planned to sign an agreement abolishing a visa requirement for diplomats of either country and will discuss a consular convention.
They signed accords for full diplomatic relations on August 23, ending a prolonged conflict that began with Croatia's secession from Serbia-led federal Yugoslavia in 1991.

Rump Yugoslavia, whose dominant republic is Serbia, also recognised Croatia's sovereignty over the last rebel Serb enclave on its territory, Eastern Slavonia, now under transitional U.N. administration.
Croatian government sources said Granic would seek an agreement with Milutinovic on when U.N. authorities should formally hand back Eastern Slavonia to Zagreb's rule.

Zagreb has reluctantly agreed to a recommendation by the U.N. administrator for an extension of the mandate into the spring of 1997 from the current expiry date of January 15, with U.N. peacekeeping troops leaving by early summer.
